help.out:
ugh — steps you can name, take out and bring back

  the daily spine (an <address> names steps — see below):
  ugh save [-m "<msg>"] [--as "<label>"]   commit your edits as a save; --as names its steps
  ugh name <address> <label>  give a label to the steps at an address
  ugh rename <label> <new>    relabel every step with a label (an existing label absorbs them)
  ugh log                     the saves, newest first, with the names on their steps
  ugh status                  what needs attention: two-version choices, unsaved edits, the plan
  ugh show <address>          its steps, the ask behind each save, what taking it out takes
  ugh find <words>            addresses whose names, subjects, definitions or asks match
  ugh undo                    invert the last mutating operation
  ugh revert <address>        take steps out of the code, holding what others stand on
  ugh restore <address>       bring steps that are out back
  ugh resolve <address> [--theirs|--ours|--apply]   the two versions a sync left; settle them
  ugh plan [<label>...] [--done]   declare names before their edits exist; report on them

  collaboration + setup:
  ugh sync [remote] [branch]  fetch + merge a teammate's work unit by unit; merge names
  ugh push [remote] [branch]  non-forcing git push; a rejection routes you to `ugh sync`
  ugh check [--tree] [--repair]   verify the op store; --repair re-derives after a history rewrite
  ugh init [path] [--horizon <ref>]   bind git + the kernel op store; mine existing history
  ugh mcp [path]              run the MCP stdio server for coding-agent clients
  ugh git <args...>           pass through to real git (refuses tree-mutating verbs)

  an <address> is a <label>, <label>@<rev>, <path>, <path>::<def>, <path>::<def>@<rev>,
  a <rev>, or <rev>..<rev>; read verbs take --json for the machine-readable ugh.api shape.
